Short title and commencement.— (1) These rules may be called the National Sports Board (Appointment, 
Salary, Allowances and other Terms and Conditions of Service of Officers and other Employees) Rules, 2026. 


They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 

Definitions.— (1) In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires, — 

“Act” means the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 (25 of 2025); 

“Board” means the National Sports Board established under sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Act; 
“Chairperson” means the Chairperson of the Board appointed under section 5 of the Act; and 
“Schedule” means the Schedules annexed to these rules. 


Words and expressions used in these rules and not defined herein, but defined in the Act, shall have the 
meaning as assigned to them in the Act. 


Application.— These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column (1) of Schedule I annexed to these 
rules. 


Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix. — The number of the said posts, their classification 
and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule I. 


Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc. — The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said 
Schedule I. 


Disqualification. — No person, - 

who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, 
exempt any person from the operation of this rule. 


Procedure for appointment by direct recruitment.— Where appointment by direct recruitment as specified 
under Schedule I is undertaken, the Central Government, in consultation with the Board, shall invite 
applications for the posts of officers and employees of the Board through advertisement and shall process 
appointments, either directly or through a recognised professional agency having adequate experience in 
recruitment for the Central Government, public sector undertakings or other similar bodies. 


Procedure for appointment on deputation basis—Where appointment by deputation 35 specified under 
Schedule I is undertaken, the Central Government, in consultation with the Board, shall invite applications for 
the posts through wide advertisement for appointments to posts as specified in Schedule I. 


Accommodation.— The officers and employees of the Board shall be eligible to House Rent Allowance in 
accordance with the extant rules of the Central Government as applicable to officers and employees drawing 
pay and allowances in the corresponding level in the pay matrix. 


Disciplinary proceedings.— The officers and employees of the Board shall be subject to disciplinary 
proceedings in accordance with the extant rules and regulations of the Central Government as applicable to 
officers and employees drawing pay and allowances in the corresponding level in the pay matrix. 


Conditions of service.— (1) The conditions of service of the officers and employees of the Board, in the 
matters for which no provision or insufficient provision is made in these rules, shall be governed by the extant 
rules and orders of the Central Government as applicable to officers and employees drawing pay and 
allowances in the corresponding level in the pay matrix.

it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with 
respect to any class or category of persons. 


13. Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, other backward classes, ex-servicemen 
and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from 
time to time in this regard.

SCHEDULE II 
[See sub-rule (4) of rule 11] 


Outdoor medical expenses. — (1) Officers and employees shall be eligible to get medical reimbursement for self 
and declared members of family. 


Explanation.— For the purpose of this clause, the expression “family” has the same meaning as assigned to it in 
the Central Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1944. 


(2) The reimbursement of outdoor medical expenses during the year shall be limited to the actual expenses or one 
month’s pay, including basic pay and dearness allowance, on 1“ January of the year whichever is lesser. 


(3) The claim should be supported by a doctor’s prescription and the original cash memos, bills for treatment by 
the doctor, purchase of medicine, and the release of increment or promotion during the year, shall not affect the 
reimbursement limit as on 1“ January. 


(4) For the officers and employees joining during the year, the annual entitlement shall be restricted on pro-rata 
basis. 


(5) The outdoor treatment shall be taken from authorised medical attendants from the panel as maintained by the 
Board. 


Indoor treatment. — (1) For the purpose of indoor treatment, the officers and employees of the Board shall be 
entitled for medical treatment at hospitals authorised by the Board in this behalf, and for this purpose, the cost of 
treatment including hospital accommodation and nursing home facility shall be as per the provisions of the 
Central Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1944 as applicable to the Central Government employees drawing 
equivalent pay. 


(2) The authorised hospitals for the purpose of paragraph (1) above shall be the same as are available to Central 
Government employees regulated by Central Services (Medical Attendance) Rules, 1944. 


(3) Treatment at authorised hospitals may be taken on the advice of the authorised medical attendants only in 
emergency.

NOTIFICATION 
Maligaon, the l3th November, 2026 
5.0. 6249(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in Ministry of Railways [N.F. 
Railway (Construction Department)], Number S.O. 4240 (E) Dtd. 29.07.2026 published on 30.07.2026 in the Gazette 
of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii) and issued under Sub-section (l) of section 20A of The 
Railways (Amendment) Act, 2008 (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, declared its 
intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule annexed to the said notification for the public purpose of 
execution, maintenance, management and operation of the Special Railway Project namely, "Buniadpur-Kaliyaganj 


New BG Railway Line Project" in the District of Dakshin Dinajpur in the State of West Bengal; 


And whereas, the substance of the said notification has been published in the daily newspapers, namely The 
Telegraph (English Edition), Dtd. 7.08.2026 and Uttarbanga Sambad (Bengali Edition) Dtd. 7.08.2026 under Sub- 
Section (4) of section — 20A of the said Act; 


And whereas, no objection has been received by the competent Authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of Sub-Section (.) of Section 20E of the said Act, the Competent Authority has 


submitted its report to the Central Government; 


And, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the power conferred 
by Sub-Section (l) of Section 20E of the said act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land specified in the 


Scheduled annexed to this notification shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And, further, in pursuance of Sub-Section (2) of Section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the Schedule Annexed to 


this notification shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

अधिकारी, कटक-पारादीप रेल लाइन दोहरीकरण परियोजना, जगतसिंहपुर को खुर्दा रोड डिवीजन के तहत कटक-पारादीप 
लाइन पर राहामा (RHMA)- बड़बंध (BDBA) स्टेशनों के बीच KM .479/5-7 पर आर.ओ.बी (रोड ओवर ब्रिज) संख्या 
CP-48 के निर्माण के संबंध में लिखित रूप में आवेदन प्रस्तुत की जाएगी तथा ऐसे आपत्ति के आधार निर्धारित किया जाएंगा 
और सक्षम प्राधिकारी, आपत्तिकर्ता को चाहे वह व्यक्तिगत रुप से हो या फिर किसी विधि व्यवसायी के माध्यम से, सुनवाई 
का अवसर देगा, और ऐसे आपत्तियां सुनने के पश्चात्‌ और आवश्यक आगे की जांच, यदि कोई हो, करने के पश्चात्‌, जैसा कि 
सक्षम प्राधिकारी आवश्यक समझे आपत्तियों को स्वीकार या अस्वीकार कर सकेगा। 


उक्त अधिनियम के 20घ की उप-धारा(2) के अंतर्गत सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी किया गया कोई भी आदेश को 
अंतिम माना जाएगा। इस अधिसूचना के अंतर्गत आने वाली भूमि की योजनाएं और अन्य विवरण उपलब्ध हैं और इच्छुक 
व्यक्ति द्वारा सक्षम प्राधिकारी के उपरोक्त कार्यालय में उनका निरीक्षण किया जा सकता है।

का.आ. 6266(अ).--- चूँकि, भारत सरकार के रेल मंत्रालय (रेलवे बोर्ड) की अधिसूचना संख्या G.S.R.639 (६), 
दिनांक 47 जुलाई, 2026 के माध्यम से - जो भारत के राजपत्र (असाधारण), भाग Il, खंड 3, उप-खंड (ii) H प्रकाशित हुई 
है - केंद्र सरकार ने रेलवे अधिनियम, 4989 (989 का 24) (जिसे आगे 'उक्त अधिनियम' कहा गया है) की धारा 200 के 
अंतर्गत, गुजरात राज्य में 'समखियाली-गांधीधाम क्राड्रपलिंग प्रोजेक्ट' (पश्चिमी रेलवे) नामक विशेष रेलवे परियोजना के 
निष्पादन, रखरखाव और संचालन के उद्देश्य से, उक्त अधिसूचना से संलग्न अनुसूची में निर्दिष्ट भूमि का अधिग्रहण करने का 
अपना इरादा घोषित किया है; 


और, चूँकि उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20/ की उप-धारा (4) के अंतर्गत, उक्त अधिसूचना का सार 25 जुलाई, 
2026 को दैनिक समाचार पत्रों - “दिव्य भास्कर” (गुजराती), “द इंडियन एक्सप्रेस” (अंग्रेज़ी) और “मेट्रो हेराल्ड” (हिंदी) - 
में प्रकाशित किया गया था; और चूँकि प्राप्त आपत्तियों पर सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा विचार किया गया और उन्हें अस्वीकार 
कर दिया गया, तथा तदनुसार आदेश पारित किए गए हैं। और, चूँकि उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20(E) की उप-धारा () 
के अनुपालन में, सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने केंद्र सरकार को अपनी रिपोर्ट सौंप दी है।

1986 की धारा 3 की उपधारा (1) और उपधारा (2) के खंड (५) के अधीन प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, अधिसूचना

का.आ. 1533(अ), तारीख 14 सितम्बर, 2006 द्वारा पर्यावरण समाघात निर्धारण अधिसूचना, 2006 (जिसे इसमें इसके 
पश्चात्‌ उक्त अधिसूचना कहा गया है) प्रकाशित की है; 


और, राज्य स्तरीय पर्यावरण समाघात निर्धारण प्राधिकरणों का गठन पर्यावरण (संरक्षण) अधिनियम, 1986 की 
धारा 3 की उपधारा (3) के अधीन, राज्य स्तर पर पर्यावरण समाघात निर्धारण अधिसूचना, 2006 के कार्यान्वयन तथा प्रवर्ग 
'ख' के अधीन आने वाले सभी प्रस्तावों पर विचार करने और पर्यावरणीय अनापत्ति प्रदान करने के लिए प्रत्यायोजित शक्तियों 
का प्रयोग करने के प्रयोजनार्थ किया गया है; 


और, राज्य स्तरीय पर्यावरण समाघात निर्धारण प्राधिकरणों ने पिछले दो दशकों के दौरान पर्यावरणीय अनापत्ति 


के आंकलन की प्रक्रिया में पर्याप्त अनुभव अर्जित किया है और राज्य स्तर पर उक्त प्रक्रिया को पर्यावरणीय अनापत्ति संबंधी 
प्रस्तावों के कुशल और पारदर्शी निपटान के लिए परिवेश पोर्टल के माध्यम से पूर्णतः ऑनलाइन भी कर दिया गया है। इसके

अतिरिक्त, केंद्रीय सरकार द्वारा पर्यावरणीय अनापत्ति प्रदान करने के लिए राज्य स्तरीय पर्यावरण समाघात निर्धारण 
प्राधिकरणों की सहायता करने के प्रयोजनार्थ अतिरिक्त राज्य स्तरीय विशेषज्ञ आंकलन समितियों का भी गठन किया जाता 


है; 


और, विशेषज्ञ आंकलन समितियों तथा राज्य स्तरीय विशेषज्ञ आंकलन समितियों में नामनिर्दिष्ट किए जाने वाले 
विशेषज्ञों के लिए अर्हताओं और अनुभव आदि से संबंधित पात्रता मानदंड समान हैं तथा वे पर्यावरण समाघात निर्धारण 
अधिसूचना, 2006 के परिशिष्ट 4 द्वारा शासित होते हैं। इस संबंध में, यह तथ्य है कि राज्य स्तरीय विशेषज्ञ आंकलन 


समितियों में विशेषज्ञ आंकलन समितियों की तुलना में समान स्तर की विशेषज्ञता उपलब्ध है; 


और, कोयला खनन परियोजनाओं के 500 हेक्टेयर तक के आंकलन के लिए राज्यों को पहले ही शक्तियां प्रत्यायोजित 
की जा चुकी हैं। गैर-कोयला खनन परियोजनाओं का पर्यावरण पर प्रभाव, कोयला खनन की तुलना में कम है। इस संबंध में, 
केंद्रीय सरकार, राज्य स्तर पर पर्यावरणीय अनापत्तियां प्रदान करने की प्रक्रिया को सुगम बनाने के लिए, गैर-कोयला खनन 
परियोजनाओं के संबंध में पर्यावरणीय अनापत्ति की प्रक्रिया का और अधिक विकेंद्रीकरण करना आवश्यक समझती है, जिसके 
लिए प्रत्यायोजन की सीमा को 250 हेक्टेयर से बढ़ाकर 500 हेक्टेयर किया जाना अपेक्षित है, जैसा कि कोयला खनन 
परियोजनाओं के मामले में किया गया है;

MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 18th November, 2026 


99.0. 6278(E).— WHEREAS, the Central Government in the erstwhile Ministry of Environment and Forests, 
in exercise of its powers under sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section (2) of section 3 of the Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986 has published the Environment Impact Assessment Notification, 2006 (hereinafter referred to 


as the said notification), vide number S.O.1533 (E), dated the 14th September, 2006 for mandating prior 
environmental clearance for certain category of projects covered in the schedule of the notification; 


And whereas, the State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authorities have been constituted under sub- 
section (3) of section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for implementation of the Environment Impact 
Assessment Notification, 2006 at State level for exercising delegated powers to consider and grant environmental 
clearance for all proposals under Category “B’; 


And whereas, the State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authorities have gained substantial 
experience over the past two decades in the environmental clearance appraisal process and the process at the State 
level has also been made completely online through the PARIVESH portal for efficient and transparent disposal of EC 
proposals. Further, the Central Government also constitutes additional State Level Expert Appraisal Committees to 
assist the State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authorities for granting environmental clearances; 


And whereas, the eligibility criteria such as qualifications and experience etc., for experts nominated in the 
Expert Appraisal Committees and State Level Expert Appraisal Committees are identical and are governed by the 
Appendix VI of the Environment Impact Assessment Notification, 2006. In this regard, it is a fact that equal level of 
expertise is available in the State Level Expert Appraisal Committees as compared to the Expert Appraisal Committees; 


And whereas, the States have already been delegated powers for appraising 500 ha., of coal mining projects. 
The impact on environment of non-coal mining projects is less as compared to coal mining. In this regard, the Central 
Government deems it necessary to further decentralise the environmental clearance process with regard to non-coal 
mining projects, by raising the threshold of delegation from 250 ha. to 500 ha., as done in coal mining projects, for 
facilitating clearances at State level; 


And whereas, the recommendations of the Expert Advisory Committee were also sought. Based on the 
recommendations of the Expert Advisory Committee, a draft notification for making amendments in the said 
notification was published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part-II, Section 3, Sub-section (1), vide number 8.0. 
4166(E) dated 27" July, 2026, inviting objections and suggestions from all the persons likely to be affected thereby, 
within a period of sixty days from the date on which copies of the Gazette containing the said draft notification were 
made available to the public and the objections and suggestions received in response to the said draft notification 
within the period of sixty days have been duly considered by the Central Government. 


Now, therefore, in exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section (2) of section 
3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (29 of 1986), read with clause (d) of sub-rule (3) of rule 5 of the 
Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986, the Central Government hereby makes the following further amendments in 
the notification of the Government of India in the erstwhile Ministry of Environment and Forests, vide number 
S.0.1533(E) dated the 14th September, 2006, namely:- 


In the said notification, in the Schedule, against item 1(a),— 
(a) in column (3), for the figures and letters “>250 ha’, the figures and letters “> 500 ha” shall be substituted; 
(b) in column (4), for the figures and letters “< 250 ha’, the figures and letters “ <500 ha” shall be substituted. 


[F. No. IA3-19/39/2025-IA HT] 
UDAY CHAUDHARI, Jt. Secy.

notification number S.O. 5189(E), dated 21 a September 2026.

प्रत्येक आपत्ति, सक्षम प्राधिकारी अर्थात भूमि अधिग्रहण के लिए सक्षम प्राधिकारी (काला) विशेष भूमि अधिग्रहण

सक्षम प्राधिकारी आवश्यक समझे आपत्तियों को स्वीकार या अस्वीकार कर सकेगा। 


उक्त अधिनियम के 20घ की उप-धारा(2) के अंतर्गत सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी किया गया कोई भी आदेश को अंतिम 
माना जाएगा। इस अधिसूचना के अंतर्गत आने वाली भूमि की योजनाएं और अन्य विवरण उपलब्ध हैं और इच्छुक व्यक्ति 
द्वारा सक्षम प्राधिकारी के उपरोक्त कार्यालय में उनका निरीक्षण किया जा सकता है।

2.1. एंकर निवेश सहायता 


2.1.1. एंकर निवेश सहायता उप-घटक का उद्देश्य ऐसे महत्वपूर्ण एंकर निवेशों को उत्प्रेरित करना है, जो निर्दिष्ट ज़ोन के 
भीतर व्यापक औद्योगिक विकास को गति प्रदान कर सकें। यह उद्यमों को पर्याप्त पूंजीगत व्यय करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करने 
पर बल देता है, जिससे मूल्यवर्धन, उत्पादक परिसंपत्तियों का सूजन और अगली पीढ़ी की विनिर्माण क्षमताओं की स्थापना 
में योगदान मिल सके। एंकर निवेश सहायता का उद्देश्य सुव्यवस्थित वित्तीय सहायता के माध्यम से ऐसी बड़ी एंकर इकाइयों 
को आकर्षित करना है, जो एकीकृत आपूर्ति शृंखलाओं का निर्माण करने, पारितंत्र के विकास को सक्षम बनाने तथा विभिन्न 
क्षेत्रों में दीर्घकालिक प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता और नवाचार को बढ़ावा देने में सक्षम हों। 

2.1.2. इस उप-घटक के अंतर्गत, निर्दिष्ट एसजीएमजेड के भीतर न्यूनतम ₹100 करोड़ का निवेश करने वाले एंकर निवेशकों 
को वित्तीय सहायता प्रदान की जाएगी। न्यूनतम निवेश की यह आवश्यकता निवेशक द्वारा स्वयं अथवा निवेशक और उसकी 
सहायक इकाइयों के संयुक्त निवेश के माध्यम से पूरी की जा सकती है। उदाहरण के लिए, कोई संस्था ₹50 करोड़ के निवेश 
से एक इकाई स्थापित कर सकती है और ₹12.5 करोड़ प्रत्येक का निवेश करने वाली चार सहायक इकाइयों को साथ ला 
सकती है, जिससे कुल F100 करोड़ की सीमा पूरी हो जाएगी। एचएस कोड (9506) के अंतर्गत आने वाले खेल उपकरणों का

New Delhi, the 17th November, 2026 
SUBJECT: KHELO INDIA SPORTS GOODS MANUFACTURING SCHEME - REG. 


F. No. J-17011/276/2026-SP-V.—The Government has approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing 
Scheme for the period F.Y. 2026-27 to F.Y. 2033-34 with the vision of developing India as a global hub for 
high-quality sports goods. 

2. Aligned with the Union Budget 2026-27 announcement of a dedicated initiative for sports goods 
that will promote manufacturing, research and innovation in equipment design and material science, the Scheme 
seeks to strengthen India’s sports goods manufacturing ecosystem. The growing participation in sports and 
fitness, supported by initiatives such as Khelo India and Fit India and hosting of the 2030 Centenary 
Commonwealth Games in India are expected to generate sustained demand for quality sports equipment and 
goods. NITI Aayog report “Realising the Export Potential of India’s Sports Equipment Manufacturing Sector”, 
also highlights the significant potential for expanding India’s sports goods manufacturing and export 
capabilities. The Scheme accordingly provides targeted support for investment, manufacturing capacity, 
technology, research, testing, skills and market development to strengthen the domestic sports goods 
manufacturing ecosystem and enhance its global competitiveness. 


3. The Scheme comprises eight components 
i. Support for setting up Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones 
ii. Anchor Investment Support 
iii. Turnover Linked Support 
iv. Support for Existing Clusters 
४. Testing and Certification Support 
Vi. Research and Skill Development Support 
vil. Support for Start-ups 
Vili. Branding and Outreach Support. 


4. The Scheme shall be implemented by the Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs & 
Sports, through the mechanisms prescribed herein and in the detailed operational guidelines. 


5. The Scheme shall be administered through an Approval and Monitoring Committee (AMC), headed 
by the Secretary, Department of Sports, which shall, inter alia, monitor the implementation and progress of the 
scheme. 

6. The approved outlay of the Scheme is %1,856.67 crore, comprising =1,416.67 crore for incentives, 
2415 crore for interventions and 225 crore for administration and implementation. 

7. The Scheme, as approved by the Union Cabinet, is hereby notified for implementation with 
immediate effect.

KHELO INDIA SPORTS GOODS MANUFACTURING SCHEME 


1. Vision 


The Vision of the scheme is “to establish India as a global hub for sports goods manufacturing”. 


The scheme envisions the development of an integrated and globally competitive sports goods 
manufacturing ecosystem, with focus on building manufacturing scale, strengthening domestic value chains and 
enabling manufacturers based in India to meet growing domestic and international demand. The Scheme seeks to 
create an enabling environment for sustained growth and competitiveness of the sports goods manufacturing 
sector. 


2. COMPONENTS OF THE SCHEME 


To fulfil the vision of the scheme, a comprehensive framework has been envisaged to support the 
development of a competitive and globally integrated sports goods manufacturing ecosystem. The scheme 
provides support across the sector, covering creation of new manufacturing capacity, expansion and strengthening 
of existing manufacturing capabilities, development of quality and technology capabilities, promotion of research 
and skills, support to emerging enterprises and facilitation of domestic and international market access. 
Accordingly, the scheme shall comprise the following components: 


1) Support for setting up Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones 
2) Anchor Investment Support 
3) Turnover Linked Support 
4) Support for Existing Clusters 
5) Testing and Certification Support 
6) Research and Skill Development Support 
7) Support for Start-ups 
8) Branding and Outreach Support 
2.1. ANCHOR INVESTMENT SUPPORT 


2.1.1. The Anchor Investment Support sub-component aims to catalyse significant anchor investments that 
can trigger broader industrial growth within designated zones. It focuses on encouraging enterprises to undertake 
substantial capital expenditure that contributes to value addition, creation of productive assets and establishment 
of next-generation manufacturing capacities. Through structured financial support, Anchor Investment Support 
seeks to attract large anchor units capable of building integrated supply chains, enabling ecosystem 
development, and driving long-term competitiveness and innovation across sectors. 


2.1.2. Under this subcomponent, financial support will be extended to Anchor Investors who invest a 
minimum of 100 crore inside designated SGMZs. This minimum investment requirement may be fulfilled 
either by the investor themselves or through the combined investment of the investor and their ancillary units. 
For example, an entity may set up a unit with an investment of %50 crore and bring four ancillary units investing 
12.5 crore each, thereby meeting the overall =100 crore threshold. For investors engaged in the manufacturing 
of sports equipment falling under HS Code (9506), the minimum investment requirement shall be = 50 crore. 


2.1.3. This benefit will also be available to globally and nationally renowned retail chains and National and 
global brands that bring their vendors and suppliers into the SGMZ. In such cases, the total investment made by 
all vendors associated with that retail chain / brand will be counted for determining eligibility under the 
subcomponent. Eligible up to 20% of CAPEX, 


subject to =100 crore per investor. However, in both these scenarios, the vendors or suppliers individually 
themselves will not be eligible for benefits. 


2.1.4. An additional incentive of up to 5 percentage points may be provided for cutting-edge products that 
are new to, or substantially under-deployed in, India, subject to an overall assistance ceiling of 7150 crore per 
investor under this provision. Such products may include advanced materials, embedded systems, engineered 
product designs, and advanced manufacturing processes that enhance performance, durability, safety, or user 
experience. Proposals seeking such support shall be evaluated against prescribed eligibility criteria and an 
evidence-based technical scorecard covering technology, manufacturing capability, IP/proprietary technology,

product performance, and strategic importance. Recommendations of the designated technical evaluation 
mechanism shall be considered by the AMC while determining eligibility for the additional incentive. 


2.1.5. Over the duration of the subcomponent, the units must achieve production equivalent to three times 
the value of the investment. 


2.1.6. | The sub-component shall be applicable only to those investors who commence investment within the 
first four years from the date of notification of a particular SGMZ, with production targets to be achieved over a 
period of up to four years post-investment, within the overall implementation period of the scheme. Additionally, 
not more than four Anchor Investors will be eligible for this benefit in each zones. 


2.1.7. Investors availing benefits under any Government of India existing Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
scheme or similar schemes will not be eligible to receive incentives under this subcomponent. 


2.1.8. Units receiving the incentive must provide an undertaking to remain in commercial production for at 
least 3 years. The Anchor Investor (along with its auxiliary units or vendors, if any) is desired to achieve 100 
jobs post commencement of the production. 


2.1.9. A total outlay of 7460 crore has been earmarked for this sub-component. Support will be available till 
the earmarked funds are exhausted. 


2.2. SUPPORT FOR SETTING UP - SPORTS GOODS MANUFACTURING ZONES 


2.2.1. Under the Support for Setting up Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) sub-component, 
financial support shall be provided for the development of designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones with 
the objective of strengthening India’s sports goods manufacturing ecosystem by enabling sports goods 
manufacturers to co-locate within a designated geography and leverage the benefits of agglomeration, shared 
infrastructure, common facilities and stronger value-chain linkages. SGMZs shall be developed through 
convergence/co-location with existing industrial infrastructure under BHAVYA and NICDC. 


2.2.2. Selection of SGMZs under the Scheme shall be undertaken through a challenge-based process, based 
on proposals submitted by eligible entities and evaluated against criteria such as availability of suitable land, 
project readiness, existing industrial ecosystem, industry participation, investment potential, employment 
generation potential, export potential and the proposed contribution to strengthening the sports goods 
manufacturing ecosystem. Initially, up to two SGMZs may be taken up in a phased manner on the 
recommendations of the Approval and Monitoring Committee (AMC), chaired by the Secretary, Department of 
Sports. Further scaling up of the SGMZ component may be considered based on 


implementation experience, demonstrated demand, performance and availability of funds Sports. 


2.2.3. Each proposed SGMZ shall preferably have a land parcel of not less than 300 acres, either within an 
existing industrial estate/industrial area or through development of a suitable greenfield zone. At least 60% of 
the land shall be earmarked for sports goods manufacturing units. The remaining area may be utilised for common 
facilities, logistics infrastructure, testing and certification facilities, worker amenities and other supporting 
infrastructure required for the development of an integrated sports goods manufacturing ecosystem. 


2.2.4. The development of the SGMZ, including industrial and common infrastructure such as trunk 
infrastructure, internal roads, utilities, industrial sheds and other park-level facilities, shall be undertaken 
through convergence with BHAVYA and NICDC, as applicable. The modalities for such convergence, 
including identification of suitable locations and funding of park-level infrastructure, shall be worked out in 
consultation with the concerned authorities. 


2.2.5. An amount of ~200 crore under the Scheme shall be utilised for the development of eligible 
infrastructure and facilities within the selected SGMZs. Such infrastructure may include facilities directly 
supporting the sports goods manufacturing value chain, such as sports goods testing and certification 
laboratories and sports product design and prototyping centres, common tooling and mould-development 
facilities, material characterisation and performance-testing facilities, demonstration facilities as well as other 
sector-specific facilities approved by the AMC. The scope of eligible sports-specific infrastructure and the 
quantum of 


support for individual SGMZs shall be determined on the basis of the approved Detailed Project Report (DPR) 
by the AMC. 


2.2.6. Financial support under the Scheme for sports-specific infrastructure shall be released in a phased 
manner against achievement of prescribed physical and financial milestones, as approved by the AMC. The 
detailed eligibility criteria, admissible components of expenditure, funding pattern, release mechanism, 
monitoring requirements and other operational modalities shall be specified in the Scheme Guidelines.

2.2.7. In addition to the SGMZs selected under this sub-component, up to two additional SGMZs may be 
notified under this provision. Eligible applicants shall be required to demarcate and delineate a land parcel of not 
less than 300 acres within their existing industrial estate for designation as an SGMZ. However, such additional 
SGMZs shall not be eligible for incentives under this sub-component. 


2.2.8. Land within an SGMZ shall be allotted only to units engaged in the manufacture of specified products 
lines under Scheme. All such allotments shall require the prior approval of the AMC and shall be subject to such 
conditions as may be specified in the Scheme Guidelines. 


2.2.9. A total financial outlay of 200 crore has been estimated under this sub-component. 


2.3. TURNOVER LINKED SUPPORT 


2.3.1. Under the Turnover Linked Support subcomponent, financial support is proposed for investors who 
commence investment within the first three years from the date of notification of the scheme. The incentive will 
be provided at the rate of 10%, 9%, 8%, 7%, and 6% of incremental turnover in consecutive years, subject to a 
cumulative ceiling of 15% of the total investment with an annual ceiling of 5% of the total investment. For 
calculating incentives, the incremental turnover in any year compared to the previous year shall be minimum of 
12%. In case of brownfield investment, incentive shall be paid on 12% increment on average turnover during the 
last 3 years; thereafter, for subsequent years, the incentives shall be paid on achieving an incremental turnover 
of 12% over the previous year. In the case of greenfield investments, minimum turnover for the first year shall be 
fixed at atleast = 0.5 crore, thereafter, for subsequent years, the incentives shall be paid on achieving an 
incremental turnover of 12% over the previous year. 


2.3.2. The incentive shall be admissible only on the net turnover of eligible products, duly verified and 
supported by certification from a Chartered Accountant based on audited financial statements and relevant sales 
records (procedural aspects shall be detailed out in guidelines). Eligible products under this category include all 
items classified under ITC (HS) code 9506. However, for investments made inside the designated SGMZ, all 
specified products lines under the scheme will also be eligible for incentives under this subcomponent. 


2.3.3. Any firm or unit investing a minimum of 10 crore (excluding land and administrative buildings) for 
the manufacturing of sports goods shall be eligible to receive benefits under this subcomponent. In addition, it is 
desired that the eligible unit to create a minimum of 30 jobs within three years after commencing operations. 


2.3.4. A total allocation of 670 crore is proposed under this subcomponent to support approximately 
150 manufacturing units expected to avail benefits under this incentive. 


2.4. SUPPORT FOR EXISTING CLUSTERS 


2.4.1. Legacy sports goods clusters such as Meerut and Jalandhar may require focused support as these 
locations evolve into mature and well-established manufacturing ecosystems. Under this sub-component, a 
comprehensive program is proposed for upgrading existing cluster infrastructure and creating common facilities 
essential for enhancing productivity and competitiveness. 


2.4.2. The total expenditure proposed under this sub-component is = 86.67 crores. The support will be 
extended subject to the condition that the respective State Governments contribute not less than 50% of the 
project cost. 


2.4.3. The interventions will be taken up based on detailed proposals submitted by the respective State 
Governments where such clusters are located. Detailed guidelines for the operationalization of this 
subcomponent will be issued once the scheme gets notified. These proposals will be examined, appraised and 
placed before the Approval and Monitoring Committee for consideration and approval. 


2.5. TESTING & CERTIFICATION SUPPORT 
2.5.1. Under the Testing & Certification Support sub-component, it is proposed to extend financial 
assistance to sports goods manufacturing companies for obtaining and renewing certifications from International 


Sports Federations. Support shall be provided up to 70% of the actual expenditure for first-time certification and 
50% of the actual expenditure for renewal. 


2.5.2. The total financial outlay proposed for this sub-component is = 105 crore.

2.6. RESEARCH & SKILL DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT 


2.6.1. Under the Research and Skill Development Support sub-component, premier educational institutions 
and research organisations shall be encouraged to establish Centres of Excellence (CoEs) within their campuses 
for undertaking research, development and innovation in sports goods manufacturing. Proposals for 
establishment of such CoEs shall be invited from eligible institutions in accordance with the prescribed 
guidelines and shall be examined and appraised by the Approval and Monitoring Committee. 


2.6.2. Co-funding of sports goods manufacturing-specific research like material science, protective 
equipments, application of infrared thermography, precision manufacturing, 3D printing etc shall also be 
undertaken under the framework of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF). 


2.6.3. Provision of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) shall be made for the establishment of dedicated testing 
laboratories for sports goods, including facilities aligned with the standards and certification requirements of 
relevant International Sports Federations. 


2.6.4. Skill development initiatives for the sports goods manufacturing sector shall be undertaken, including 
development of training programmes, skilling interventions, and collaboration with industry and training 
institutions to create a skilled manpower base for the sector. 


2.6.5. An overall outlay of 210 crore is proposed for this sub-component, inter alia, for establishment of 
Centres of Excellence (CoEs), support under the ANRF, provision of VGF for testing laboratories, and skill 
development initiatives. 


2.7. SUPPORT FOR START-UPS 


2.7.1. The Start-up Support component shall be implemented through convergence with the existing 
DPIIT/Startup India framework, with a dedicated sports goods manufacturing priority/challenge window to 
support start-ups engaged in product innovation, design, prototyping, advanced materials, testing and validation, 
and manufacturing technologies. The Department of Sports shall, in consultation with DPIIT, identify priority 
challenge areas and facilitate participation of eligible start-ups through the existing Startup India ecosystem. 
Financial support of up to 220 lakh per eligible start-up shall be provided through the identified Startup 
India/DPIIT framework, subject to the applicable guidelines and funding modalities. The total financial outlay 
proposed for this component is = 50 crores. 


2.8. BRANDING & OUTREACH SUPPORT 


Promotion of the Indian sports goods manufacturing sector is critical for enhancing global competitiveness, 
strengthening market access, and attracting investments. The sub component provides for structured 
promotion of the sector through outreach activities, international exhibitions, and branding & PR initiatives. 
An overall budgetary outlay of =50 crore has been proposed under this component for a period of 5 years. 


2.8.1. GLOBAL SPORTS GOODS FAIRS & INTERNATIONAL EXHIBITIONS 


The sub component shall support organization of international level global sports expo in India. These 
interventions will provide a platform for domestic manufacturers to showcase capabilities, facilitate B2B 
engagements, and strengthen export linkages. 


2.8.2. OUTREACH ACTIVITIES 
The sub-component shall support outreach activities, including investor outreach, roadshows, and engagement 
through bilateral and multilateral trade platforms related to sports. BSM and RBSM-related activities may be 


aligned with, or leveraged through, the Export Promotion Mission, wherever feasible, to avoid duplication 
of efforts and enhance the overall effectiveness of export promotion initiatives.

2.8.3. BRAND INDIA CAMPAIGN 


Under this sub-component, the Department of Sports shall coordinate with the Department of Commerce to 
promote a unified ‘Brand India’ presence for Indian sports goods and equipment in international markets. A 
dedicated branding campaign may be undertaken at select global sports goods exhibitions and other high- 
visibility platforms to position India as a globally competitive hub for sports goods manufacturing. Such 
activities shall complement and not duplicate branding and marketing support available under the Export 
Promotion Mission. 


3. IDENTIFICATION OF PRODUCT LINES: 


3.1. Description of Products: 


3.1.1. All sports equipment classified under HS Code 9506, along with other items primarily intended and 
used in sports, including para sports, and physical fitness, such as racing bicycles, sports nutrition products, 
sports gear, sportswear, athleisure footwear, headgear, accessories, sports flooring, etc shall be eligible for 
benefits under the Scheme. 


3.1.2. Eligibility shall also extend to prototypes, calibration and measuring instruments, digital and display 
equipment, specialised software platforms, and other products which are predominantly used in or commonly 
associated with sports activities. 


3.1.3. The Scheme shall further cover the manufacturing of key machinery, components, inputs, and sub- 
assemblies that are primarily utilised in the production of the aforementioned sports goods. 


3.2. APPROVAL MECHANISM: 


3.2.1. In cases where any question of eligibility determination arises with respect to a particular product, 
the matter shall be placed before the Approval and Monitoring Committee (AMC) constituted under the Scheme 
for consideration and appropriate clarification.

proposals and if found in order, will approve such proposals and disburse the financial support. The committee 
will include senior officials, not below the rank of Joint Secretary, from NITI Aayog, Commerce, DPIIT, CBIC, 
IFD, MSME, Concerned State Government Representative or Other Central Ministries/Autonomous 
Bodies/Agencies Representatives, 3 Industry/Academia nominees. 


The following are the key functional areas of the AMC for effective implementation and oversight of the Scheme: 
e Examine applications recommended by PMA and make appropriate decisions under the scheme 
e Approve and review the list of eligible products under target segments etc., periodically. 


e Monitor the progress of approved applicants in terms of investment, employment generation, 
production and domestic value addition 


e Monitor and review of the progress made under the scheme, including roundtable conference 
with the beneficiaries 


e Recommend amendments to scheme guidelines, including changes to target segments, 
incentive rates, etc. 


e Incase of any clarification regarding the provisions of the scheme, the decision of the AMC shall be 
final 


e In case of force majeure events, it may recommend modifications or withdrawal of specific 
scheme provisions.

setting up of a dedicated Project Monitoring Agency (PMA)/ Project Implementing Unit (PIU) for efficient 
administration of this scheme.

Detailed operational guidelines for each sub-component of the Scheme including the process for inviting 
applications and the mechanism for grievance redressal will be formulated and notified by the Department 
of Sports. These guidelines will outline the criteria for selection of eligible companies/units, procedures for 
effective monitoring of the Scheme, modalities for release of incentives and the coordination framework.

नियंत्रक एवं महालेखापरीक्षक , संघ लोक सेवा आयोग , आयुष मंत्रालय के सभी सम्बद्ध / अधीनस्थ कार्यालय / सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उपक्रम आदि 
तथा भारत सरकार के सभी मंत्रालयों / विभागों और राज्य सरकारों एवं संघ राज्य प्रशासनों को भेजी जाए । 

यह भी आदेश दिया जाता है कि संकल्प को सामान्य जानकारी के लिए भारत सरकार के राजपत्र में प्रकाशित किया जाए ।

सामान्य जीवन में हम वापस आ गए हैं । हमने पांच प्रमुख शहरों में ऑफ लाइन मोड में बीमांकिक दिवस 2022 मनाया है । 


लगभग 2 वर्षों के बाद महामारी के पश्चात हमने पहला ऑफलाइन कार्यक्रम , 37 वां इंडिया फेलोशिप सेमिनार ( आईएफएस ) आयोजित 
किया , ताकि सदस्यों को व्यक्तिगत रूप से जुड़ने और बातचीत करने में सक्षम बनाया जा सके । तब से , आईएआई ने दोहरा दृष्टिकोण 
अपनाया है- कुछ कार्यक्रमों को ऑनलाइन मोड में और कुछ को ऑफलाइन इन – पर्सन मोड में संचालित किया जा रहा है । हमने दिसंबर 
2022 बीमांकिक परीक्षा ऑफलाइन मोड में आयोजित करने की घोषणा की है ।

अधिक दक्षता और हितधारकों के लिए बेहतर सेवा लाने के लिए वर्ष के दौरान संस्थान के प्रशासनिक ढांचे को फिर से डिजाइन किया 
गया है । बीमांकिक समुदाय की ओर से , मैं बीमांकिक पेशे के लिए विकास और परिवर्तन लाने हेतु समर्पित कार्य और पूरे दिल से 
संलग्नता के लिए आईएआई कर्मचारियों के लिए अपनी प्रशंसा दर्ज करना चाहता हूं । इनमें से कुछ कार्यक्रमों में उच्च स्तरीय प्रशिक्षण 
कार्यक्रम , बेहतर सदस्य सेवाएं , नई वेबसाइट का विकास , आंतरिक पत्रिका का डिजिटलीकरण , बीमांकिक अध्ययन सामग्री के विकास की 
शुरुआत और सम्मेलनों और संगोष्ठियों का सफल संचालन शामिल हैं । 


संस्थान निवर्तमान सदस्य को इस पेशे में उनके अपार योगदान के लिए धन्यवाद देता है । संस्थान परिषद , अनुशासन समिति , क्यूआरबी 
और अपीलीय प्राधिकरण में नए सदस्यों का स्वागत करता है और मानता है कि उनके अनुभव और विचारों से संस्थान को अत्यधिक लाभ 
होगा । 

वित्तीय स्थिति 

— 

2021-22 की वित्तीय स्थिति इस अवधि के दौरान संस्थान के कार्य करने के मजबूत तरीके को दर्शाती है । वित्त वर्ष 2021-22 में फीस 
और सेमिनार से होने वाली आय वित्तीय वर्ष 2020 - 21 के 12.50 करोड़ रुपये से बढ़कर 13.95 करोड़ रुपये हो गई है । निवल अधिशेष 
वित्त वर्ष 2020-21 के 4.53 करोड़ रुपये की तुलना में वित्तीय वर्ष 2021-22 में बढ़कर 7.88 करोड़ रुपये हो गया है । संस्थान का निवेश 
भी वित्त वर्ष 2020-21 के 47.20 करोड़ रुपये से बढ़कर वित्त वर्ष 2021-22 में 57.66 करोड़ रुपये हो गया है । 


विस्तृत वित्तीय विवरण के साथ - साथ प्रासंगिक अनुसूचियां और लेखाओं की टिप्पणियां इस रिपोर्ट के भाग हैं । 

एक सांविधिक लेखा परीक्षक के रूप में मैसर्स एम एस एम एम एसोसिएट्स ने इन लेखाओं की लेखा परीक्षा की है और 31 मार्च 2022 
की स्थिति के अनुसार संस्थान के कामकाज की भारत में आमतौर पर स्वीकृत सभी लेखांकन सिद्धांतों के साथ अनुरूपता को प्रमाणित 
किया है ।

चाहता हूं जिन्होंने वर्ष के दौरान निर्धारित कई लक्ष्यों और विजनों को प्राप्त करने के लिए मेरे साथ कड़ी मेहनत की ।

करने के लिए एक शैक्षिक सहायता योजना है । 31 मार्च 2022 तक ऐसे छात्रों की कुल संख्या 11 थी । आईएआई ने वित्तीय वर्ष 
2021-22 में ऐसे छात्रों को कुल 1,97,500 रुपये की प्रतिपूर्ति की । इसमें वार्षिक सदस्यता शुल्क के मद में 20,000 रुपये , अध्ययन 
सामग्री की लागत के मद में 1,01,500 रुपये , परीक्षा शुल्क 66,000 रुपये और कोचिंग शुल्क के मद में 10,000 रुपये शामिल हैं ।

सार्वजनिक भलाई को आगे बढ़ाने की अपार क्षमता का उदाहरण दिया । बीमांकिक दिवस 2021 दो घंटे का आभासी सत्र था जिसमें 
लगभग 500–600 प्रतिनिधियों ने भाग लिया । मुख्य भाषण हमारे माननीय मुख्य अतिथि श्री अमित अग्रवाल , अपर सचिव , वित्तीय सेवा 
विभाग , वित्त मंत्रालय , भारत सरकार द्वारा दिया गया था । श्री नागेंद्र डी राव , अध्यक्ष , भारतीय कंपनी सचिव संस्थान ( आईसीएसआई ) इस 
आयोजन के लिए हमारे विशेष आमंत्रित थे । बीमांकिक बिरादरी के कुछ दिग्गज जैसे श्री डी के पंडित , के ए पंडित के भागीदार , श्री हेमंत 
कुमार पाहुजा , प्रधान , वैश्विक सेवाओं में बीमांकिक समारोह के नेता श्री जी एल सरमा , मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी - हनोवर रक एसई ,

पर्याप्त लेखांकन अभिलेखों का रखरखाव ; उपयुक्त लेखांकन नीतियों का चयन और अनुप्रयोग , ऐसे निर्णय करना और आकलन करना जो 
यूक्तिसंगत और विवेकपूर्ण हो ; और पर्याप्त आंतरिक वित्तीय नियंत्रण की रूपरेखा बनाना , क्रियान्वयन करना और रखरखाव करना जो ऐसे 
वित्तीय विवरणों को तैयार करने और प्रस्तुत करने , जो एक वास्तविक और निष्पक्ष स्थिति दर्शाता हो और जो तथ्यात्मक मिथ्या बयानी से 
मुक्त हो , चाहे वह धोखाधड़ी के कारण हो या त्रुटिवश के लिए प्रसांगिक लेखांकन अभिलेखों की सटीकता और संपूर्णता सुनिश्चित करने 
के लिए प्रभावी रूप से प्रचालन में थे , शामिल है । 

लेखा परीक्षक की जिम्मेदारी 

हमारी जिम्मेदारी अपनी लेखा परीक्षा पर आधारित इन वित्तीय विवरणों पर हमारी राय व्यक्त करना है । हमने अपनी लेखा परीक्षा 
भारत में सामान्य रूप से स्वीकृत लेखा परीक्षा मानकों के अनुसार की है । इन मानकों में यह अपेक्षा की गई है कि हम इस बारे में 
तक्रसंगत आश्वासन प्राप्त करने के लिए लेखा परीक्षा की योजना इस प्रकार बनाएं और लेखा परीक्षा करें कि वित्तीय विवरण 
तथ्यात्मक मिथ्या कथन से मुक्त हो ।

किसी लेखा परीक्षा में वित्तीय विवरणों में धनराशियों और प्रकटनों के बारे में लेखा परीक्षा साक्ष्य प्राप्त करने के लिए प्रक्रिया विधियों का 
निष्पादन शामिल होता है । चयनित प्रक्रिया विधियां लेखा परीक्षक के विवेक पर निर्भर करती हैं , जिसमें वित्तीय विवरणों की तथ्यात्मक 
मिथ्या बयानी , चाहे वह धोखाधड़ी के कारण हो या त्रुटिवश के जोखिमों का आकलन शामिल है । इन जोखिमों के आकलन करने में , लेखा 
परीक्षक उपयुक्त लेखा परीक्षा प्रक्रियाओं की अभिकल्पना करने हेतु संस्थान के वित्तीय विवरणों की तैयारी के प्रासंगिक आंतरिक वित्तीय 
नियंत्रण पर विचार करता है जो उन परिस्थितियों के लिए यथोचित हो , सही और निष्पक्ष स्थिति प्रस्तुत करता है , परंतु संस्थान में 
वित्तीय रिपोर्टिंग पर पर्याप्त आंतरिक नियंत्रण प्रणाली होने या नहीं होने और ऐसे नियंत्रणों की ऑपरेटिंग प्रभावकारिता पर एक मत व्यक्त 
करने के लिए नहीं । एक लेखा परीक्षा में प्रयुक्त लेखांकन नीतियों के औचित्य और प्रबंधन द्वारा लेखांकन आकलनों की विश्वसनीयता का 
मूल्यांकन करना भी शामिल होता है , साथ ही वित्तीय विवरणों की समग्र प्रस्तुति का आकलन करना भी शामिल होता है ।

2. राजस्व मान्यता 

क ) प्रवेश शुल्क :

ख ) सदस्यता शुल्क : 

वर्ष में प्राप्त सदस्यता शुल्क वास्तविक प्राप्ति आधार पर आय के रूप में माना गया है ।

है ।

1. PRESIDENT'S UPDATE ON THE ACTIVTIES OF THE INSTITUTE 


Subhendu Kumar Bal 
President 

Success is not final , failure is not fatal : it is the courage to continue that counts- Winston Churchill 


It's my great pleasure and privilege to present the Annual Report and Accounts of the Institute of Actuaries of India for 
Financial Year 2021-22 . 


Our Country has managed the pandemic very well even though the world is still facing challenges of Pandemic . India has 
vaccinated more than 210 crores doses of vaccine which is a significant milestone achieved . India has not only managed the 
Covid - 19 very well but also has made significant progress by achieving the 5th largest economy in the World . 


India is celebrating Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav this year . This is the year of reveling rising India , rejoicing the arrival of India 
on the global stage . In the midst of the Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav , IAI is celebrating this year with a spirit of pride , positivity , 
and confidence in the future . 


The Institute of Actuaries of India also has shown a lot of resilience and done remarkable progress in achieving the vision of 
IAI 2.0 . 

Landmark Year 

The year 2021-22 has been landmark year for the Institute by achieving several landmarks along with the new innovative 
initiatives . 


Three years back we celebrated 75 years of the Actuarial profession in India . As a part of the celebration , we had promised to 
ourselves to reinvent the actuarial profession in India . To fulfill the promise and to redeem our tryst with the future , last year 
IAI established the vision of IAI 2.0 . I am happy to share that we have made significant progress so far in this regard . 

Engaging Stakeholders 


To serve the actuarial community better , we are closely engaged with stakeholders like Government authorities , IRDAI and 
other regulators , global actuarial bodies , media , and others . 


During the year we selected a Media Partner to help us digitize our communication , engage the media , and manage our social 
media . 


I am happy to report that IAI has joined the expert committee constituted by IRDAI to draw the roadmap for the 
implementation of IND AS 117 .

Digital Experience 

The transition to the Actuary India digital format is aligned with the vision IAI 2.0 . During the year we have achieved a 
landmark by successfully launching a multimedia - based Digital Actuary India magazine . This magazine has come with a new 
digital avatar with audio - visual features along with podcast and interviews , polls and survey , technical articles and life stories . 


In addition , there are event reports , culture , Trivia , Humour and Puzzles , all built on a high- technology creative platforms . Our 
magazine has received kudos , appreciation , and extremely positive feedback from various stakeholders .

Last year , on Actuaries Day , IAI announced the establishment of the Olympiad in Actuarial 
Science for Indian Students ( OASIS ) to spread awareness about Actuarial Science among 
Generation Z. This also helps to increase awareness about actuarial profession among 
parents , teachers and public at large . 


OASIS 


OASIS is designed to test the theoretical concepts and practical applications of Commercial 
Mathematics , Calculus , Statistics , Modelling and Data Science taught to the students from 
Class 9 to Class 12. It aims to develop critical thinking capabilities and Higher Order 
Analytical Skills . It is divided into two phases - Pre - OASIS 


Examination for students from Class 9 & 10 & OASIS Examination for students of Class 
11 & 12 . 


The OASIS was formally launched on 27 May 2022 at Varanasi by conducting the 1st seminar for principals & teachers of 
schools in the Varanasi District . Institute has conducted many seminars in various schools & Colleges . 


As part of the Azadi ka Amrit Mahatsov celebration initiated by the Government of India , IAI initiated dialogue with CBSE 
for collaboration 1 ) Increase Awareness about Actuarial Science 2 ) to Appoint 750 Actuarial Science Ambassadors across all 
CBSE schools , and 3 ) to Inspire students to participate in Olympiad and Awards by reaching out to around 7.5 lacs secondary 
and higher secondary students

IAI - The Talent And Innovation Partner Of The Industry 


It is a different world today , and yesterday's skillset and mindset aren't adequate to deal with it . 

We have come a long way from the spreadsheets - dominated world to the more powerful data analytic tools and actuarial skills 
requirements . 


The demand and opportunities for actuarial talent are changing . The actuarial talent is in demand beyond the traditional areas , 
from Insuretech and Fintech , from technology companies to the BFSI industry , from all other industries .

To channel and grow the demand for actuarial talent , the institute is re - focussing and repositioning itself as a talent and 
innovation partner for the industry and employers . To help engage actuarial talent better , we have launched a corporate outreach 
program . Since the launch , we have met over 15 employers to understand their needs and identify the skill gaps . Accordingly , 
we have appointed a placement officer in the Institute and providing Job oriented trainings for skill enhancement of our 
members and students . 

Job - Oriented Training Programme 

During the year , IAI has conducted many high - end training programs , including R - Webinar series , Python - programming 
language , Machine learning - Re - defining role of actuaries , A capsule training for IFRS 17 implementation , The Microsoft 
Macros & VBA and Practices of Employee and Group Benefit valuation . More than 1500 members , including fellows , have 
benefitted from this training . 


In addition , many coaching , guidance , and support programs have been conducted which helped many candidates to perform 
better in examinations . 


Iai New Education Curriculum 

The new education policy and India specific curriculum of IAI is expected to bring in new subjects which are relevant for the 
future . This includes specialisation in Data Science and Banking & Financial Services . 


Inspired by the Aatmanirbhar Bharat , IAI has initiated development of India Specific Actuarial Study Material . The work on 
the preparation of the study material is in progress . 

Accreditation Of University / Institute 

IAI has established the accreditation program for universities and academic institutes . 

The Accreditation Programme will enable universities / Institutes to obtain recognition of their courses aligned with the IAI 
curriculum and learning objectives and to leverage educational and trainings services . 


Among many things , it will also benefit students undertaking a Programme , with an agreement , not only by gaining exemption 
from some of the IAI professional examination but also by developing a broader skillset that will be relevant in a competitive 
job market . 

The Apex Accreditation Steering Group ( AASG ) has been constituted . 

New Indian Individual Annuitant's Mortality Table ( 2012- 15 ) 

I am pleased to inform you that new Indian Individual Annuitant's Mortality Table ( 2012- 15 ) , within the provisions of sub 
regulations 2 of Regulation 5 under Schedule II ( Valuation of Liabilities- Life Insurance ) of Insurance Regulatory and 
Development Authority of India ( Assets , Liabilities , and Solvency Margin of Life Insurance Business ) Regulations , 2016 is 
published and is effective from 1 April 2021. This standard table has been published after due consultation and concurrence of 
the Insurance Regulatory Development Authority of India ( IRDAI ) . 

Review of Actuaries Act 2006 


The Actuaries Act was passed in the year 2006. With the experience gained from the last 15 years or so and to address the 
challenges faced by Actuarial Profession , the Actuaries Act Review Task Force has been constituted with members from the 
profession and experts from the fields of Accountancy and Law . The Taskforce shall look into international best practices at 
the actuarial bodies and best practices of similar statutory bodies in India . The final report of the task force with 
recommendations to meet challenges of the future and to take the profession to the next stage is expected soon . 

Virtual Actuarial Conclave ( VAC ) 2022 : 

Inspired and encouraged by the grand success of Virtual Actuarial Conclave 2021 , the Institute repeated the signature event of 
the year in the same virtual format during the month of February 2022. VAC 2022 created new records with over 3,300 
registrations , 71 global and Indian speakers and 34 partners .

We are Reverting to Offline Mode 

I am happy to report that , IAI has risen to the challenge of Covid - 19 to serve the actuarial community . IAI successfully 
conducted two Virtual Actuarial Conclaves , five online Actuarial Examination diets , six online ACET Examination , and many 
Educational Guidance , support and training programs . 


Since we celebrate Actuaries Day last year , the pandemic situation eased and bounced back to normal life early this year . We 
have celebrated Actuaries Day 2022 in five major cities in the off line mode . 


After almost 2 years , we conducted the first offline program post - pandemic , the 37th India Fellowship Seminar ( IFS ) to enable 
members to connect and interact in person . Since then , IAI has adopted the dual approach- to conduct some programs in online 
mode and some in offline in - person mode . We have announced the December 2022 actuarial examination in the offline mode . 

Re - invigorated , Re - purposed IAI Administration with Relevant Skills 

The Administrative structure of the Institute have been re - designed during the year in order to bring in greater efficiency and 
better service for the stakeholders . . On behalf of the Actuarial community , I would like to put on record my appreciation for 
the IAI staff for their dedicated work and whole - hearted engagements for bringing in developments and changes for the 
actuarial profession . Some of the engagements include , high - end training programs , improved member services , development 
of new website , digitization of in - house magazine , initiation of development of actuarial study material and successful 
conduction of conferences and seminars . 


The Institute thanks the outgoing member for their immense contribution to the profession . Institute welcomes the new 
members to the Council , Disciplinary Committee , QRB and Appellate Authority & believes their experience and thoughts will 
immensely benefit the Institute . 

Financials 


The financials of 2021-22 reflect the robust way the Institute has functioned during the period . Income from fees and seminar 
in FY 2021-22 has increased to Rs.13.95 Cr from Rs . 12.50 Cr in FY 2020-21 . Net surplus in FY 2021-22 has increased to 
Rs.7.88 Cr from Rs.4.53 Cr in FY 2020-21 . Investment of the Institute increased to Rs.57.66 Cr in FY 2021-22 from Rs.47.20 
Cr in FY 2020-21 . 


The detailed financials along with relevant schedules and notes to accounts are forming part of this report . 

M / S M.S.M.M Associates as a statutory auditor audited the accounts and certified the conformity with all accounting principles 
generally accepted in India of the state of affairs of the Institute as on 31st March , 2022 . 


I would like to give big thanks to all the Council members , Members of Section 21 committees , Members of Section 26 
committee , Members of the Quality Review Board , Members of Appellate Authority , Advisory group members and incredible 
volunteers who have supported whole heartedly during the year . 


I would also like to thank the staff members of the Institute who worked very hard with me to achieve several landmarks and 
visions set during the year . 


We have achieved successes in many landmarks and some of set goals are under progress , which I am sure that we are going 
to achieve in the coming year with the supports from all of you . I would like to end my update by remembering the below quote 
of Mr. Martin Luther King Jr. 


" If you can't fly then run , if you can't run then walk , if you can't walk then crawl , but whatever you do you have to keep moving 
forward . "

Functions of the Council 

The duty of carrying out the functions under the provisions of this Act shall be vested in the Council . 

In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power , the functions of the Council shall include : 

the holding of examination of the candidates for enrolment and specifying fees therefor ; 

the specifying of qualifications for entry in the register ; 

the recognition of foreign qualifications and training for the purposes of enrolment ; 

the granting of or refusal to grant the certificate of practice under this Act ; 

the maintenance and publication of a register of persons qualified to practice as Actuaries ; 

the levy and collection of fees from members , students , examinees and other persons ; 

the removal of names from the register and the restoration to the register of names which have been removed ; 

the regulation and maintenance of the status and standard of professional qualifications of members of the Institute ; 
to issue guidelines for the observance of the members , including the student members ; 

to receive gifts , grants , donations or benefactions from the Central or State Governments and to receive bequests , 
donations and transfer of movable or immovable properties from testators , donors or transferors , as the case may be ;

REPORT ON EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT AND TRAINING 

I. ONLINE GUIDANCE & SUPPORT FOR EXAMINATIONS 

The online guidance and support for students appearing for examinations extended for higher order few subjects under CP , SP 
and SA level in addition to all core technical subjects . Under core technical subjects , online classes for all practical examinations 
viz . , CS1B , CS2B , CM1B , CM2B and R - Statistical software have also been offered during the period . Lot of flexibility has 
been brought in by offering recorded videos along with LIVE sessions till the date of examinations . Around 800 students 
benefited by way of interacting with expert faculty members within the lowest fee structure .

Report on Virtual Actuarial Conference 2022 ( VAC 2022 ) 

The 2nd Virtual Actuarial Conference was held from 10th to 12th February , 2022. A task force of 14 members from the 
actuarial profession under the Chairmanship of Honorary Secretary Ms. Preeti Chandrashekhar was constituted well in 
advance on 9th September 2021 , who together with Mr. Subhendu Bal , President , IAI and the entire IAI staff members 
accomplished the task of planning , organizing and conducting the program in a proper phased out manner with lots of 
brain storming . 71 speakers from different countries like India , USA , UK , South Africa , Australia shared their knowledge 
in their areas of expertise . VAC 2022 was a grand success with 3000+ registrations from all across the globe . 


VAC 2022 was centred around the theme " Preparing for a New Era- Decoding Disruption " & covered topics like 
Managing Consumers ' needs and expectations in BANI world , IFRS 17 , Decoding Longevity , Nurturing Actuarial 
Talent , COVID19 : Managing Demographic Risk , De - risking the Balance Sheet & many more . 


VAC 2022 had two special chief guests for the event , Shri Supratim Bandyopadhyay Chairperson , PFRDA & Ms. 
Roseanne Harris , President International Actuarial Association . 


Cherry on the cake was the appreciation received from 

Shri Narendra Modi Ji Hon'ble Prime Minister of India as mentioned in the letter sent by PMO dated 9th February 2022 
" As business professionals , Actuaries help develop & utilize statistical & financial models , enabling institutions & 
individuals to solve complex financial issues , as well as arrive at better informed financial decisions . They assess the 
financial impact of uncertain events in the future and analyse risk management in various fields " 


Smt . Nirmala Sitharaman Ji Hon'ble Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs in the letter sent by Finance minister's 
office dated 12th February 2022 wherein it was written " Congratulations to the Institute of Actuaries of India for 
organizing the 2nd Virtual Actuarial Conclave ( VAC 2022 ) . The theme of the conclave " Preparing for a New Era 
Decoding Disruption " is very pertinent for the present times . "

Actuaries Day is celebrated on 21st August every year . The Actuaries Day is a day for drawing inspiration from the multifaceted

accounting principles generally accepted in India . This responsibility also includes maintenance of adequate accounting records

implementation and maintenance of adequate internal financial controls that were operating effectively for ensuring the

PROVISIONS 


A provision is recognised when an enterprise has a present obligation as a result of past events : it is probable that an 
outflow of resources will be required to settle the obligation , in respect of which a reliable estimate can be made . 
Provisions are not discounted to its present value and are determined based on best estimates required to settle the 
obligations at the Balance Sheet Date . These are reviewed at each Balance Sheet Date and adjusted to reflect the 
current best estimates .

CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS 

Contingent liability is a possible obligation that arises from past events and the existence of which will be confirmed

Institute , or is a present obligations that arises from past event but is not recognised because either it is not probable 
that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation , or a reliable 
estimate of the amount of the obligation cannot be made . Contingent liabilities are disclosed and not recognised . 
Contingent assets are neither recognised not disclosed .
